daily_brief: US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are heading to Kyiv on Sunday following three hours of talks with Vladimir Putin in Moscow, marking the first visit by Trump's top negotiators to Ukraine's capital as both sides agreed to a three-day pause on strikes against each other's capitals [BBC], [France 24], [RFI]. Meanwhile, the US-Iran conflict escalated sharply as both nations traded retaliatory attacks on ships in the Gulf, with the US 'permanently disabling' two Iranian oil tankers and Iran claiming strikes on US-affiliated vessels in response [BBC], [Globe and Mail]. In Germany, voters in Saxony-Anhalt head to polls where the far-right AfD is polling above 40 percent and could secure its first state-level power since World War II, a development being closely watched across Europe [BBC], [Le Monde], [RFI], [Financial Times]. The Anak Krakatau volcano eruption has stranded over 150,000 passengers after forcing the closure of six Indonesian airports including Jakarta's main international hub [BBC], [Globe and Mail]. Israeli air strikes killed four people in southern Lebanon despite an ongoing ceasefire, with Israel claiming the strikes responded to Hezbollah drone launches [France 24], [Al Jazeera].

top_stories.headline: US Envoys Head to Kyiv After Three-Hour Kremlin Talks with Putin
bullets: Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner held three hours of closed-door talks with Vladimir Putin at the Kremlin on Saturday, described by Russian officials as 'constructive and extremely frank'
Both Putin and Zelensky agreed to halt strikes on each other's capitals for three days during the negotiations
The envoys are expected to arrive in Kyiv on Sunday, marking their first visit to Ukraine's capital since Trump returned to office
Kremlin adviser Yuri Ushakov stated discussions covered economic issues and potential 'mutually beneficial Russian-American projects' beyond the Ukraine crisis

sources.name: BBC World
sources.framing_note: Emphasized both sides giving 'broadly positive remarks' and focused on diplomatic process

sources.name: France 24
sources.framing_note: Headline described talks as 'a bad sign' suggesting more skeptical framing

sources.name: RFI English
sources.framing_note: Noted Zelensky accused Russia of trying to disrupt visit with airport strikes

sources.name: Globe and Mail
sources.framing_note: Highlighted that Washington's push has 'lost momentum' due to focus on Iran war

top_stories.headline: US and Iran Trade Retaliatory Ship Attacks as Gulf Conflict Escalates
bullets: US military 'permanently disabled' two Iranian oil tankers near Kharg Island and 'completely destroyed' a third in the Gulf of Oman
Iran's state media claimed Tehran attacked three US-affiliated vessels and three oil tankers travelling an 'unauthorized' route through the Strait of Hormuz in response
US Central Command said an aircraft carrier and destroyer 'successfully evaded' multiple Iranian attacks with no American casualties
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth warned: 'If Iran shoots at US ships, we will destroy (and sink) their oil tankers'

sources.name: BBC World
sources.framing_note: Provided detailed account of both sides' claims and noted Trump dismissed conflict as 'small potatoes'

sources.name: Globe and Mail
sources.framing_note: Emphasized this continues 'six months of on-again, off-again war' and noted negotiations have collapsed

sources.name: France 24
sources.framing_note: Limited content available but confirmed Iran claims strike on US ship

top_stories.headline: Germany's Far-Right AfD Poised for Historic State Election Victory in Saxony-Anhalt
bullets: AfD polling above 40 percent in Saxony-Anhalt, approximately 15-20 points ahead of Chancellor Merz's CDU
35-year-old lead candidate Ulrich Siegmund could become AfD's first state premier if party wins outright majority
An absolute majority would mark the first time a far-right party has held state-level power in Germany's post-war era
The party has campaigned on tougher immigration rules, deportation of undocumented migrants, and closer ties with Russia

sources.name: BBC Europe
sources.framing_note: Described it as an election 'that could change German history' and called it 'a point of serious peril' for opponents

sources.name: RFI English
sources.framing_note: Noted Der Spiegel called Siegmund 'Germany's most dangerous man'

sources.name: Le Monde
sources.framing_note: Limited content but confirmed AfD expected to win

sources.name: Globe and Mail
sources.framing_note: Emphasized vote is 'barometer for embattled Chancellor Friedrich Merz'

top_stories.headline: Anak Krakatau Eruption Strands 150,000 Passengers as Indonesia Closes Six Airports
bullets: Jakarta's Soekarno-Hatta International Airport and five other airports suspended operations due to volcanic ash reaching up to 50,000 feet
At least 467 flights affected including international routes to Singapore, Doha, Sydney and Kuala Lumpur
Volcano began erupting late Friday night with continuous seismic activity, lava fountains, and booming sounds; two more eruptions occurred early Sunday
Transport ministry urged airlines to expedite refunds and provide timely information to avoid airport overcrowding

sources.name: BBC World
sources.framing_note: Led with human impact angle of 150,000 stranded passengers

sources.name: Globe and Mail
sources.framing_note: Focused on operational details and government response measures

top_stories.headline: Israeli Strikes Kill Four in Southern Lebanon Despite Ceasefire
bullets: Israeli air strikes on southern Lebanon killed four people including two women and wounded at least 20 others
Israel's military said strikes were response to Hezbollah launching two drones at Israeli soldiers in the self-declared 'security zone'
Strikes hit multiple locations including Nabatieh, Arab Salim, Nabatieh al-Fawqa and Kfar Reman
Lebanon's health ministry said the death toll was provisional; Israel issued its first 'evacuation' notice in Lebanon in several weeks

sources.name: France 24
sources.framing_note: Described as 'latest escalation despite a months-long ceasefire'

sources.name: Al Jazeera
sources.framing_note: Emphasized Israel violated 'ceasefire agreement reached in June' and described Israeli 'security zone' as a claim 'inside Lebanese territory'
